author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Detroit City FC aims to extend perfect start against Union FC Macomb
text:
Detroit City FC will travel to Macomb on May 27 for a USL W League match against Union FC Macomb, seeking to continue its unbeaten run at the top of the Great Lakes Division. The match is scheduled for 7 p.m. at Barnabo Field.
Le Rouge currently holds a 2–0–0 record with six points, making it the only team in the division with a perfect points-per-game mark. Union FC Macomb sits fourth in the standings, having earned three points from three matches and holding a 1–2–0 record. This fixture sets up an early-season contest between the division leaders and a team looking to move into the upper half of the table.
Detroit City FC began its season with a 2–1 away win over AFC Ann Arbor, featuring goals from Kaiya Stewart and Drew Martin. The team then secured a last-minute victory at Keyworth Stadium when Lily Jeakle converted a penalty to defeat Kalamazoo FC 1–0. Detroit has scored three goals while conceding only one so far this season, reflecting strong defensive organization and timely offensive execution.
Union FC Macomb opened its campaign with two narrow losses on the road but responded by earning its first win in a 1–0 result against AFC Ann Arbor on Memorial Day. Andie Jones scored for Union while goalkeeper Kealey Titmuss kept a clean sheet. The match also marked the league debut of Hannah Yu, who is among the youngest athletes in USL W League at age fifteen.
Key storylines include Detroit’s ability to secure results away from home following their earlier road win, and whether they can maintain momentum as early pace-setters in their division. Jeakle’s stoppage-time winner demonstrated Detroit’s composure late in matches—a quality that may be tested again if Wednesday’s contest remains close. Meanwhile, Union’s recent shutout victory suggests improved defensive structure as they look to challenge Detroit’s perfect start.
Detroit City FC is known for its exciting matchday atmosphere and community-driven soccer success; it promotes unity and local pride through inclusive culture and supporter engagement; utilizes Keyworth Stadium for home matches; has gained recognition as one of North America’s most discussed soccer teams due to passionate supporters; aims to meet soccer demand in Detroit while fostering community through sport; and operates under co-founders including CEO Sean Mann and Chief Creative Officer Alex Wright, according to the official website.
